input: My Discord bot isn't responding to messages. What should I check?
ideal: Check these in order: 1) message_content intent — must be enabled both in code (intents.message_content = True) AND in Discord Developer Portal > Bot > Privileged Gateway Intents. This is the most common cause. 2) Bot mentions — if your bot only responds to @mentions, check that the mention detection is correct: client.user in message.mentions. 3) Bot ignores its own messages — if message.author.bot: return must be present to prevent infinite loops. 4) Ollama is running — confirm with curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags. 5) DISCORD_TOKEN is loaded — print(bool(DISCORD_TOKEN)) at startup to verify .env is loading. 6) The model is pulled — ollama pull <model-name>.
rubric: Should list message_content intent as a top suspect. Should mention Developer Portal toggle. Should cover Ollama connectivity. Should be a structured checklist.

input: How do I make slash commands appear in Discord? I've registered them in code but they don't show up.
ideal: Slash commands require syncing with Discord's API. You must call await tree.sync() in your on_ready event. Two modes: 1) Global sync: await tree.sync() — takes up to 1 hour to propagate. 2) Guild sync (instant, for development): MY_GUILD = discord.Object(id=YOUR_GUILD_ID); await tree.sync(guild=MY_GUILD). Also check: the bot must have the applications.commands OAuth2 scope when invited — re-invite with the correct scope if needed. In your bot invite URL, include both bot and applications.commands in the scope. After syncing, type / in your server — the commands should appear.
rubric: Should explain that sync is required. Should give both global and guild sync options. Should mention that guild sync is instant. Should mention applications.commands scope in invite URL.

input: How do I make my Discord bot remember context from earlier in the conversation?
ideal: Store conversation history per user in a rolling buffer. Use defaultdict(lambda: deque(maxlen=10)) keyed by user ID. On each message: 1) Add user message to history: conversations[user_id].append({'role': 'user', 'content': text}). 2) Query Ollama with system prompt + history: messages = [{'role': 'system', 'content': SYSTEM_PROMPT}, *list(conversations[user_id])]. 3) Add assistant reply to history: conversations[user_id].append({'role': 'assistant', 'content': reply}). maxlen=10 keeps the 10 most recent messages — older ones drop off automatically. History is per-user and in-memory (resets on restart). For persistence, write to SQLite. Provide a /clear command so users can reset their own history.
rubric: Should show deque with maxlen. Should show the message format (role/content). Should show inserting system prompt before history. Should mention adding both user and assistant messages. Should mention /clear command.

input: What's the right way to handle long responses that exceed Discord's 2000 character limit?
ideal: Two approaches: 1) Split into chunks: chunks = [reply[i:i+1990] for i in range(0, len(reply), 1990)]; await message.reply(chunks[0]); then send remaining chunks with await message.channel.send(chunk). Use 1990 not 2000 to leave safety margin. Better: split at newlines to avoid cutting mid-sentence: split_at = text.rfind('\n', 0, 1990). 2) Use embeds: discord.Embed allows up to 4096 characters in the description field — embed = discord.Embed(description=reply[:4096]); await message.reply(embed=embed). Prevention: add a length constraint to your system prompt ('Keep responses under 400 words unless asked for more detail') to reduce how often this happens.
rubric: Should give a working code approach for chunking. Should mention the 2000 char limit. Should mention embeds as an alternative (4096 char limit). Should recommend preventing long responses via system prompt.
